subject: Rebaseline: AcmeCorp POC scope & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC follow-up: success criteria & next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for a productive demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC moving: 

Call recap / agreed scope:
- Validate Redwood inference for customer-support summarization (10k monthly sessions).
- Measure latency (p50/p95) and cost per 1k tokens for our recommended pod configs.
- Evaluate integration with Acme's existing analytics pipeline for quality metrics.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Average summary helpfulness >= 4.2/5 on the sample set of 500 conversations (annotation by Acme QA).
2) p95 serving latency <= 600ms for 95% of requests during core business hours.
3) End-to-end integration with analytics capturing latency + model confidence in the dashboard.

Timeline & owners:
- Week 0 (this week): share evaluation dataset & access details (Samantha / Raj) — RECEIVED
- Week 1: Redwood deploys POC model + integration (Marissa / Camila)
- Weeks 2-3: Evaluation run, annotations, and initial metrics (Acme QA + Redwood)
- Week 4: Review and go/no-go decision

Attachments: poc-success-metrics.xlsx (template for metrics), acme-architecture.png (high-level integration).

Can you confirm the success criteria above and whether the timeline works for your team? Also confirm primary owner for annotations on Acme side (Raj or another).

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC follow-up: success criteria & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. We're aligned on most items, but one update from our side: during the call Raj asked to add an additional use case to the POC — automated escalation detection (identifying conversations that should be routed to Tier 2).

Impact on success criteria:
- For escalation detection, we'd like to track precision/recall on a labeled set of ~250 escalation examples. Target: precision >= 0.85 and recall >= 0.80.

Impact on timeline: adding this use case will likely require an extra week to label and incorporate signals into the evaluation. Can we rebaseline to extend the evaluation window by one week (so decision in Week 5)?

Owner on our side: Raj will lead annotations for escalation detection; I'll coordinate logistics.

If Redwood is okay with updating the scope and timeline, let's adjust the plan and confirm resources.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Product, AcmeCorp
samantha@acme-corp.com

Subject: Re: POC follow-up: success criteria & next steps (scope update)

Hi Samantha / Raj —

Thanks — this is reasonable and we can accommodate the escalation detection use case. Per Camila's availability and our infra plan, here's a proposed rebaseline to include the new use case and keep deliverables clear: 

Updated success criteria (two buckets):
A) Summarization (original):
- Helpfulness >= 4.2/5 on 500 conversation sample
- p95 latency <= 600ms

B) Escalation detection (new):
- Labeled set of 250 examples with precision >= 0.85 and recall >= 0.80
- False positive rate <= 6% on a production-like sample

Updated timeline (dates approximate):
- Week 0 (wk of Feb 23): dataset & access — complete
- Week 1 (wk of Mar 2): Redwood deploys initial model for summarization + basic metrics capture (Camila)
- Week 2 (wk of Mar 9): Acme completes labeling for escalation detection (Raj)
- Week 3 (wk of Mar 16): Redwood runs combined evaluation for both use cases and compiles results (Camila + Marissa)
- Week 4 (wk of Mar 23): Final review and decision (extended one week from original)

Resourcing / next steps:
- Camila: will own deployment and evaluation runs (I'll loop Camila into access details).
- Raj: will own labeling for escalation detection — please share labeling conventions and a sample set by Mar 4.
- Marissa: will monitor project timeline and coordinate stakeholder reviews.

Notes: adding the escalation use case increases the evaluation complexity but not the infra cost materially — we can run the combined evaluation in a single POC environment. Attached is an updated metrics template; I'll post the updated HubSpot deal note after you confirm.

Can you confirm Raj is OK with the labeling cadence and that Mar 23 as final review works for Acme?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick update from the engineering side.

We can support the additional escalation detection use case. A few implementation notes and confirmation of ownership: 
- Deployment: I'll provision a shared POC namespace with separate routes for summarization and detection so we can measure metrics independently.
- Data/access: Marissa — please send API keys and the sample dataset link; Samantha / Raj, add the labeled examples to the Drive folder (link below) by Mar 4 so we can schedule runs.
- Evaluation plan: we'll run three evaluation passes (smoke, full-run, and production validation) — expect the full-run to take ~48 hours once labeling is complete.
- Resources: Logan, can you confirm GPU pool allocation for weeks of Mar 2 and Mar 9? We expect a single V100-equivalent host for the test runs.

I've updated the shared Drive with an evaluation checklist and runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e?usp=sharing

Next steps / action items:
- Samantha / Raj: confirm labeling cadence and upload -> Due: Mar 4
- Logan: confirm GPU allocation -> Due: Mar 6
- Marissa: confirm HubSpot note & updated deal timeline -> Due: Mar 6

I'll kick off the smoke test as soon as labeling is uploaded and API access confirmed.

Cheers,
